options.plan: Upstream release 26.8.0; commercial support not assessed
options.region: Operator-selected hosting; storage destinations not verified
options.configuration: Public browser/native OIDC clients; code + S256 PKCE; exact redirects; no service accounts, SAML, SCIM or brokers

conditions: Register separate public clients with Client authentication off, Standard Flow enabled and PKCE method S256; a blank PKCE method does not require PKCE.
Register narrowly scoped redirect URIs and only the browser origins needed by the integration; no full production redirect wildcard.
Validate issuer, state, nonce and callback handling in the consuming application; documentation does not demonstrate a configured deployment.
This public-client scope excludes confidential BFF clients, service-account grants, SAML, SCIM and upstream identity brokers.

evidence.summary: Release-pinned client settings describe public versus confidential clients, the Standard Flow switch, exact redirect matching, browser origins and an explicit S256 PKCE requirement. This is a configuration proposal, not a deployment check.

conditions: Limit this proposal to a public browser OIDC client using Authorization Code with S256 PKCE and exact registered redirects.
Keep client credentials out of browser code; test callback, token handling, origin policy and browser restrictions independently.
Documented browser login does not verify local-session logout, deprovisioning, phishing resistance or a confidential BFF implementation.

evidence.summary: The release-pinned grant guide describes Authorization Code redirects and identifies web applications as a target. It does not establish application-side security controls or live browser interoperability.

conditions: Limit this proposal to a public native/mobile OIDC client using Authorization Code with S256 PKCE; do not treat a distributed client secret as confidential.
Application prerequisite: use an external user-agent and an OS-bound return URI under RFC 8252, not a credential-capturing embedded WebView.
Register and test the actual platform callback, issuer/state/nonce validation and token storage; no mobile SDK, OS integration or universal-link ownership has been verified.
The grant guide's user-agent wording is not evidence that an embedded WebView meets RFC 8252; this proposal does not certify mobile assurance or lifecycle enforcement.

evidence.summary: The release-pinned grant guide includes native and mobile applications in the Authorization Code use cases. External-browser and callback requirements are explicit application prerequisites, not tested platform compatibility or a mobile SDK guarantee.
